question: The coordinates of four points $P(1,2)$, $Q(-2,3)$, $R(0,-1)$ and $S(4,1)$ are to be represented by a matrix $A=[a_{ij}]$ in which each column represents one point, the first row contains the $x$-coordinates and the second row contains the $y$-coordinates. Form the matrix $A$, determine its order and number of elements, identify $a_{23}$ and $a_{14}$, and hence obtain $A'$ explaining the information represented by each row of $A'$.
explanation:
Formation of the Matrix

Since each column represents one point and the first and second rows contain the $x$-coordinates and $y$-coordinates respectively, $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-2&0&4\\2&3&-1&1\end{bmatrix}$$ The matrix has $2$ rows and $4$ columns. Therefore, its order is $2\times4$ and the number of elements is $2\times4=8$. Using the notation $A=[a_{ij}]$, the element $a_{23}$ lies in the second row and third column, so $a_{23}=-1$. Also, $a_{14}$ lies in the first row and fourth column, so $a_{14}=4$.

Transpose

The transpose is obtained by interchanging the rows and columns of $A$. Thus, $$A'=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-2&3\\0&-1\\4&1\end{bmatrix}$$ The order of $A'$ is $4\times2$. Each row of $A'$ now contains the two coordinates of one of the points. Thus its rows represent $P(1,2)$, $Q(-2,3)$, $R(0,-1)$ and $S(4,1)$ respectively. Hence, the given coordinate information is represented consistently by both $A$ and its transpose.
